LESSON: FURNITURE AT HOME

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: My Home
Topic 3.2: Furniture at Home
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Furniture at Home, part of My Home in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have furniture at home?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Furniture at Home together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: learner speaks clearly and effectively when naming the furniture used at home.

• Learning to learn: learner learns independently when reading pictures of furniture used at home.

59

Values:
• Responsibility: learner cares and handles furniture used at home appropriately.

• Integrity: learner enhances self-discipline when using furniture used at home.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Disaster risk reduction: learner observes safety precautions when handling and taking care of furniture used at home.

Link to other learning area:

Furniture at home relate to sides of objects in Mathematical Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Approved learning support materials, picture/ picture cut-outs about furniture used at home, theme based communication board

about furniture used at home, Photographs/ Newspaper cuttings/ Flash cards/ charts with legible print and appropriate colour

contrast furniture used at home, heavy gauge Manilla papers, Adapted Pencils, marker pens and crayons with enhanced grip,

splints for holding affected arm of arms with repetitive movements/ hand stabilizers, pencil grips, adapted digital devices

(computers/ video players/ speakers/ audio-visual recorders/ smart phones) with appropriate accessibility features and

software, foot-boards, slates, slant board, adhesive such as masking tape,

Related Service Providers: Physiotherapists, Occupational Therapists, Speech Therapists, Resource Persons, Learner Support

a) identify furniture used at

home,

at home.


  -  In purposive groups or pairs,

learners are guided to talk/ share

ideas about furniture used at

home (chair, table, stool, bed,

cupboard, shelves orally

(through residual speec
h) / by

writing/ pointing or through total

communication.


  -  In purposive groups or pairs,

learners are strategically

positioned or preferentially

seated and guided to observe

drawn pictures of furniture used

at home. The pictures should be

of clear colour contrast and

placed on a surface or displayed

at a place that is accessible by

each learner. For learners with

repetitive body movement

(tremor
s) , the pictures should be

mounted on cardboards or

secured on the table tops or slant

boards using any preferred

adhesive such as masking tape.

54


  -  Learners are guided to picture

read furniture used at home. The

pictures should be of clear

colour contrast and placed on a

surface or displayed at a place

that is accessible by each

learner. For learners with

repetitive body movement

(tremor
s) , the pictures should be

mounted on cardboards or

secured on the table tops or slant

boards using any preferred

adhesive such as masking tape.


  -  Learners are appropriately

positioned/ seated and guided to

colour furniture used at home.

Learners with manipulation

difficulties could use any

functional part of the body,

appropriate Assistive technology

adapted pencils or crayons with

grips to do the colouring with

physical support. They could use

slant boards, book holders and

pencil grips to perform the task.

Learners with tremors could

55

require splinting of the most

affected limb or use of hand

stabilizers. In severe cases,

learners with manipulation

difficulties could describe orally

the materials, choice of colour

and procedure for colouring as a

physical assistant does the actual

drawing under their instruction.


  -  Learners are appropriately

positioned/ seated on devices

with worktops/ table tops at

suitable heigh and guided to join

dots of furniture used at home.

They could use slant boards,

book holders and pencil with

grips to perform the task.

Learners with tremors could

require splinting of the most

affected limb or use of hand

stabilizers. In severe cases,

learners with manipulation

difficulties could describe orally

the process of joining the dots as

a physical assistant does the

actual task.

56


  -  Learners are strategically

positioned or preferentially

seated on positioning/ seating

devices whose worktops/ table

tops are at a suitable height and

guided to model furniture used

at home using any functional

part of the body/ appropriate

Assistive technology such as a

mould of a chair. Learners with

severe manipulation difficulties

could describe the materials

used and the procedure for

modelling as a physical assistant

does the actual modelling under

their instructions.


  -  Learners are guided to care for

and handle furniture used at

home appropriately using any

functional part of the body/

appropriate Assistive technology

for manipulation with physical

support. Learners with severe

manipulation difficulties could

describe how to carry out the

task orally as a physical assistant

57

does the actual task.


  -  In purposive groups or pairs,

learners are strategically

positioned or preferentially

seated on positioning/ seating

devices whose worktops/ table

tops are at a suitable height and

guided to watch video clips on

furniture used at home. Learners

with short stature, difficulties in

vision, difficulties in hearing as

well as those on positioning

devices should be seated in close

proximity to the source of video.

The screen light/ glare should be

appropriately adjusted to suit

learners with difficulties in

vision. Learners with

manipulation difficulties could

use any functional part of the

body/ appropriate Assistive

technology such as head/ mouth

pointers to operate the adapted

digital devices with physical

support.

58


  -  Learners are appropriately

positioned and guided to sing/

hum/ dance to the tune of songs

about furniture used at home, or

point the words in the lyrics or

tap/ clap/ stump rhythmically as

peers sing along


  -  Learners are guided to play

singing games on furniture used

at home, with roles assigned in

line with individual learner’s

uniqueness. Learners with brittle

bone disease should be assigned

less vigorous tasks. Those with

difficulties in movement could

be supported to use mobility

devices as they play. Learners

such as those with sickle cell

anaemia and those with cardiac

conditions should be monitored

not to get into strenuous

performance.
